item.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption reviews contemporary corruption risks and integrity issues to help public agencies target prevention efforts.
item.support: it is a scan of the contemporary factors that contribute to corruption and other serious forms of misconduct.

item.text: It draws on published research, its own data and stakeholder consultation, covering recruitment, procurement, regulation and government-funded non-government organisations.
item.support: the Commission has researched contemporary publications, including the reports of counterpart agencies, analysed its own data, consulted stakeholders

item.text: The Commission identifies weak information management, unrestricted authority and governance failures as recurring factors associated with corruption.
item.support: Some of the factors that stand out include poor management of information, unfettered discretion or authority and governance failings.

item.text: The Commission advises prevention efforts to target processes where individuals control decisions alone or can hide or manipulate information.
item.support: corruption prevention efforts should focus on processes where individuals have the ability to exercise unilateral control over key decisions

item.quote: The Commission’s key observation is that many agencies are falling short of acceptable employment screening practices.
